name: Xiaofan Yu
title: Assistant Professor (tenure-track; joined July 2025)
researchAreas: Efficient learned multi-UAV tracking and planning
fitReason: Recently hired Assistant Professor with concrete robot-AI methods and an explicit external-master visitor route. A method-focused, lower-physical-confidence alternative; the published minimum duration makes it less convenient for a roughly eight-week visit.

physicalEvidence.summary: DroneFL combines frozen YOLOv11n features and a small transformer with federated updates and trajectory optimization for coordinated UAV tracking. The full 2025 paper evaluates flight/tracking in Gazebo; its Raspberry Pi 5 tests measure runtime, power and communication, not actual drone flight. Full 2026 HyperLiDAR studies adaptive LiDAR segmentation on SemanticKITTI and nuScenes; these recorded datasets and accelerator throughput estimates do not establish learned real-vehicle execution. Current UC Merced robot apparatus and access remain unverified.

shortVisit.status: inquiry-only · 最低3–6个月；降低短期优先级
shortVisit.summary: The current Visiting Students section explicitly accepts students enrolled in outside undergraduate/MS programs from US or international institutions, with a research proposal and self/external funding, and lists UCM J1 support. It requires a minimum 3–6-month commitment and an application 3–6 months before arrival. This is a standing invitation, not a confirmed summer2027 place. The closed 2025–26 PhD recruitment cycle is a separate category and must not be described as no visitors or no summer interns.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive multi-UAV neural prediction/planning and learned spatial perception, alongside broader embedded AI.
scoreReasons.physical: Inspected robot evaluation is simulated or recorded-data; Raspberry Pi/ASIC runtime is not robot execution.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Explicit outside-master visitor invitation, limited credit because minimum 3–6 months and no confirmed summer2027 availability.
scoreReasons.freshness: Dated April 2026 spatial-AI paper and June 2026 robotics publication acceptance; current standing visitor page.
